I'm not a lawyer, and honestly nobody can promise you'll win. The result depends on your proof and on what the Commission decides. What I can say is that a refund dispute over Rs 9,000 headphones is the kind of case the District Consumer Commission hears. Filing is free at this amount, you can do it yourself on e-Jagriti, and it must be within 2 years of the problem.

Your chances are better if you have the bill, proof of the defect, and proof you asked for a refund and were refused. Before filing, try the seller's grievance officer and the National Consumer Helpline (1915). Many cases settle there.

When did you buy them, and what went wrong?
